description: Send a draft as it stood at the revision you pass: now, at sendAt (up to 29 days ahead), or delaySecs from when we receive the call (up to 300 seconds, on our clock, so a wrong clock on your side does not shorten the wait). It goes through the same checks as every send (the suppression list, the mailbox, its daily cap and the plan's daily sends), and the draft is marked sent. A new message also needs a fresh check that says its address can receive mail (run check_email_address first; preview_draft shows where the address stands): an address not checked yet, out of date or found invalid answers 409 and nothing is sent, and one the check couldn't confirm (risky, or it couldn't tell) answers 409 `recipientNeedsReview` until you pass `recipientReviewed: true`. A reply to mail you received needs no check, and a reply to mail you sent stops only for an address found invalid. A merge field left in the subject or message, such as `{{ company }}`, answers 409 `draftUnfilled` and nothing is sent (not one a reply's subject kept from the message it answers). The same call again answers the same send. A revision someone has since changed answers 409 and sends nothing. The answer is the send as reserved, or as scheduled: read it with get_send for the outcome, and cancel it with cancel_send until it starts going out. An email scheduled with sendAt meets the mailbox's gap, the daily caps and the address check when it is due, so a check still running when you schedule it can finish by then. If a check refuses it then (a paused mailbox, a used-up cap, an address that isn't cleared), it is canceled and says why. delaySecs is only time to cancel the email, so its address needs the check done now. An owner may limit the API key you call with: to some mailboxes or campaigns, to outreach or transactional email, and to a number of emails a day or in all. Anything outside those limits answers 403 and nothing is sent: `details.scope` names the limit (`keyMailbox`, `keyCampaign`, `keyStream` or `keyTotal`). When the key has sent all its emails for today, it answers 429 with `details.scope: "keyDay"`, `resetAt` and a Retry-After header. A key can't read or change its own limits: ask a workspace owner. A scheduled email meets the key's limits again when it is due. New messages and replies to your own sent mail are cold direct outreach. They carry `List-Unsubscribe` and, over HTTPS, `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, with a link for this send's To address. No footer is added. They meet the mailbox's domain grace, health rest and cold ceiling. A refusal names `details.scope`: `mailboxDomain` or `mailboxHealth` (409, `details.resetAt` null), `mailboxColdRest` (409, its fixed end), or `mailboxColdDay` (429, the workspace's midnight and Retry-After). Scheduled promotion checks again; claim stops a rest that began later. Every 15 minutes, 0.1% complaints or 5% bounces over at least 50 cold direct sends in 7 days rests the mailbox for 72 hours. Only sends since the last trip count. `get_mailbox` returns `coldRest` and the visible problem; `mailbox.failed` and `mailbox.recovered` mark the trip and lift. Three automatic pause days in 30 days can restrict the workspace, unless staff pinned its posture. Replies to mail received, tests, transactional mail, warmup and seed do not get these headers or cold gates.

delaySecs.description: Send it this many seconds after we receive the call, 1 to 300, counted on our clock rather than yours. Until then, cancel_send stops it and gives you the draft back. Pass sendAt or delaySecs, not both.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

recipientReviewed.description: true: send even though the address check couldn't confirm the address (risky, or it couldn't tell), because you looked and accept that. It never sends to an address found invalid, one on the suppression list, or one whose check is missing or out of date.

revision.description: The revision you read. If the draft changed since, nothing is sent (409).

sendAt.description: When to send it, as an ISO 8601 date and time with its offset, up to 29 days ahead. Left out, or already past, it goes now.

name: send_draft
title: Send a draft
